text: On million-token chats the cost shape changes: in 10 lead sessions of one project (USD 1,005 at list prices) cache re-reads were 38% of cost, cache writes 31%, output 31%; helpers were 56% of the spend (median USD 7.10, 58 turns, 29 minutes). The earlier measure (re-reads 7% of cost) holds only for short sessions. A turn at 500K context costs 2.5 times a turn at 200K.

Claude Code cache kinds, measured from transcripts and confirmed in the docs: on a subscription the main chat writes 1-hour cache (2x input), subagents write 5-minute cache (1.25x) and start at about 7K tokens; settings promptCacheTtl / subagentPromptCacheTtl choose it. A helper that waits over 5 minutes on one command rewrites its whole context.

For a GDScript project, parse changed scripts with gdtoolkit in one Python process before any engine run and in a pre-push hook: 0.3 s for changed files, 25 s for 1,451 scripts, no false alarm on a green tree, and on its first run it found a merge's stray else that had stopped three chats' tests. Godot's --check-only cannot check a whole project.

When several chats build in parallel and only the lead may edit shared files, requests written as prose make the dearest, largest-context chat retype them one by one and the backlog keeps the tree red. Ask for each request as a tested patch file (git diff from the requester's worktree plus the test that proves it); the lead applies it with one command.

Before taking the lead from a handover, compare the branch you were started on with every remote branch's last commit time: the handover and state on main can be hours behind a lead branch that is hundreds of commits ahead, and acting from main's state would redo or contradict finished work.

From inside a cloud session an environment cannot be created with unrestricted network (only an allowlist) and variables that steer the runtime (for example CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW) are refused; both are the owner's clicks in the environment's settings.

Claude Code, official docs 2026-11-26: .claudeignore does not exist (permissions deny Read rules do the job); plain stdout of a PostToolUse hook never reaches the model (exit 2 with stderr, or JSON additionalContext, does); plugins and LSP servers cannot be installed from a committed file in cloud sessions.

The owner starts every GitHub Actions run himself. A session never starts, cancels or reruns a workflow and never pushes in order to start one; it prepares the commit, says it is ready, and gives the exact clicks.
